title: Tunable continuous-batcher: mixed-length stratification & memory-aware KV packing
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description:
Problem: In production we observe increased OOMs and p95 latency regressions for workloads with mixed prompt/response shapes (short prompts with long generations and vice versa). The current continuous-batcher equally mixes requests and uses a global KV policy which causes transient KV memory spikes and ineffective slot packing under skewed length distributions.

Goal: Implement a tunable batching scheduler that stratifies the continuous queue by request shape, applies memory-aware KV packing and adaptive slot compaction, and exposes knobs for per-model KV-window sizing so we reduce OOMs, improve tail latencies, and preserve throughput without increasing cost materially.

Scope: scheduler codepath + runtime config surfaces + telemetry + canary rollout. This ticket covers design, implementation, experiments, and a 5% canary in dedicated pools. Follow-up tickets will handle UI knobs in Console and specific client SDK hints.

Non-goals: training changes, model quantization improvements (except where necessary for packing), changes to client API surface.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for mixed-shape synthetic trace decreases by >= 15% compared to baseline with same throughput
OOMs per 100k requests drop to zero or < 0.1 for canary traffic
GPU memory headroom variance reduced by >= 25% during bursts
No regression (>2%) in tokens/sec throughput at steady state
Config knobs documented and accessible via runtime config; default safe values enabled
updates: 2026-03-08: Kickoff — collected production sampling of sequence-length histograms across models; identified 3 dominant shapes: short->long, long->short, balanced. Added sampling pipeline to runtime to emit per-request shape tag.

2026-03-10: Prototype stratified queue implemented: requests now hashed into 3 strata based on (prompt_length, expected_max_response) percentiles. Early microbench shows reduced cross-length contention but increased slot fragmentation on skewed loads.
2026-03-11: Introduced adaptive slot compaction that attempts to compact small tail slots into spare capacity windows when KV overhead allows. Reduced fragmentation metric in bench by ~18%.

2026-03-12: Added memory-hysteresis threshold (low/med/high) to gate aggressive compaction vs conservative eviction; decided to default to conservative for hosted tier and allow aggressive for dedicated/private via runtime flag.

2026-03-13: Experiment plan finalized — synthetic traces, production replay on staging, and 5% canary. Metrics and dashboards cloned: batch composition, kv-resident-bytes, eviction-rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, oom_count, tokens_per_sec.
2026-03-14: Began implementation of per-model kv-window tuning: runtime will maintain per-model target_kv_windows and a decay-based estimator for active KV entries; initial unit tests passing.
Next: finalize scheduling heuristics for mixing strata under low load to avoid throughput cliffs; prepare canary rollout playbook and runbooks for on-call.
Blocked: need updated kernel memory profiling tool (ENG-15742 follow-up) to get fine-grained GPU allocation deltas; coordinating with infra team.
review_comments: PM (Jin Park): Good to see customer-facing acceptance metrics. Please add a cost-sensitivity check — measure if adaptive compaction increases per-token GPU-time/cycle cost.
Design (Marta Liu): Ensure strata decision is explainable for debugging; include reason codes in batch traces (e.g., STRATA_SHORT_LONG) to aid postmortems.
Infra (Liam O'Connor): For canary, use a dedicated small pool with identical GPU types to avoid noisy neighbor effects. Also require a hard abort if OOM rate exceeds threshold.
implementation_notes: Stratification: classify requests into 'short->long', 'long->short', 'balanced' using sampled percentiles (10th,50th,90th) of prompt_length and historical response_length for the client/model.

Scheduler: maintain independent sliding-slot queues per strata; allow controlled cross-strata melding when headroom and latency targets permit. Use fast-path for single-request slots to reduce enqueuing overhead.
KV packing: when constructing a slot, compute projected kv_bytes = sum(kv_per_seq * seq_len) and ensure projected memory + current_resident < kv_budget_per_gpu - hysteresis_margin.
Eviction policy: implement 'eviction budget' per slot — prefer LRU within a slot but avoid global churn by bounding evictions per second.
Telemetry: tag each batch with strata id, projected_kv_bytes, actual_kv_bytes_post_send, eviction_count. Emit metrics at batch and GPU host levels.
Config knobs: strata_threshold_percentiles, kv_budget_per_gpu, hysteresis_margin_bytes, eviction_budget_per_sec, aggressive_compaction_enable (bool), per_model_kv_window_override.
Testing: unit tests for slot compaction logic, integration tests using production replay traces, stress test to trigger OOM edge cases in staging before canary.
Canary: 5% traffic on dedicated pool with abort conditions: oom_count > 0 for 5 consecutive minutes OR p95 latency regression > 25% for 10m window. Rollback automation via infra runbook.
testing_plan: Create synthetic trace set that mixes 60% short->long, 30% balanced, 10% long->short. Run tests across model sizes (1B, 7B, 70B) and precisions (fp16, int8).
Replay week-long production sample on staging with new scheduler to validate steady-state and burst behavior.
A/B canary: route 5% production traffic to canary pool and run side-by-side for 48 hours with automated result comparison and alerting rules.
Run targeted OOM injection tests (simulate KV spikes) to validate eviction budget and rollback safety nets.
